input.new_string:
## Orchestrator agent-management policy

Added 2026-08-29 after a live incident: 8 per-card standing agents
(`gym-stat-mock`, `gym-stat-uireview-auth`, `gym-stat-uireview-flows`,
`gym-stat-machinetypeeditor`, `gym-stat-accountgymforms`, `gym-stat-numericoverflow`,
`gym-stat-floorplanux`, `gym-stat-privacypolicy`) were found sitting idle for anywhere from
90 minutes to 9+ hours, never stopped after their assigned card's work was finished (or never
progressing past launch at all). Root cause for several of them, confirmed by reading their raw
session screens: each was launched with `/remote-control` enabled, and got stuck mid-handshake
("`/rc` connecting…", never resolving) before ever reaching its actual work prompt — the card
assigned to that agent never got touched at all, while the agent itself sat there indefinitely
consuming a session, a claude.ai remote-control connection, and (for Grok/Codex ones) a
provider session.

Two rules for this orchestrator going forward:

- **Do not create always-on standing agents for per-card work.** A dedicated agent spun up to
  do ONE card's work is not furniture — it is a worker that has a start and an end. Stop it
  (via the Antiphon agent `/stop` API) once its card is merged/closed or once its report has
  been reviewed and accepted, whichever this orchestrator's own workflow uses as "done." Do not
  leave it running "just in case" or because stopping it wasn't part of the original launch
  script. `AlwaysOn` is reserved for genuinely long-lived standing roles (this orchestrator
  itself), never for a one-card worker.
- **Do not enable remote control (`/remote-control`) on a launch unless the operator explicitly
  asked for it for that specific agent.** It is not needed for the orchestrator's own dispatch
  loop to read a worker's report, and — per the incident above — it is an active liability: a
  stuck remote-control handshake can silently prevent the agent from ever reaching its actual
  work, with no visible error, for hours.
